props.name: lead
props.description: A short hairline dash before the text. Ignored when `icon` is set.

props.name: icon
props.description: Decorative icon before the text, about 1.25× the text size. Hidden from assistive tech.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colours only the rule or icon (text.brand, accent.text or the feedback fg role). The label stays text.subtle.

props.name: as
props.description: p above a heading or section; span inside other text or flex rows.

props.name: children
props.description: Two to four words. Write it in sentence case; CSS sets the capitals.

notes: Not interactive and not a heading: it names a group without adding to the document outline. Put the real heading after it.
Capitals come from text-transform, so screen readers read the words, not letters. Write the source in sentence case.
The rule and icon are aria-hidden decoration; tone never carries meaning on its own.
Tracking is --strata-font-tracking-caps: 0.08em for Latin pairs and 0 for Arabic-capable pairs, so joined scripts are never letter-spaced.

do: Use one eyebrow per block, directly above the heading or figure it introduces.
Keep it to a few words: a category, a date, a status.
Use tone on the rule or icon to hint at the kind of note (accent for onboarding, warning for a caveat).
dont: Don't use it as a heading or as the only label for a section: screen readers skip it in the outline.
Don't write the text in capitals in the source.
Don't stack several eyebrows or put one above every line: it stops reading as a kicker.
